question.text: Vaidya Debt AIF (Category II) is valuing a INR 1,000 par bond held in portfolio. Coupon = 10% p.a. (annual), 4 years to maturity. Required yield (YTM) = 8%. Use PVA factor at 8%, 4 yrs = 3.312 and PV factor at 8%, 4 yrs = 0.735. Fair value of the bond?

explanation.text: The Logic: V = Coupon x PVA(r,n) + F x PV(r,n) = 100 x 3.312 + 1000 x 0.735 = 331.20 + 735.00 = INR 1,066.20. Per Section 14.2, when YTM < coupon, bond trades at premium (price > par). The Trap: INR 1,000 assumes par (ignores discount rate differential). INR 950.40 uses required yield > coupon logic (wrong direction). INR 1,100 miscounts principal. Cross-Exam Context: X-B (IA L2) and XV (Research Analyst) test the same bond pricing; XIX-C applies to debt-AIF portfolio marking where the FIMMDA/FBIL-derived YTM is the market-discount input. Manager's Pro-Tip: For Cat II debt AIFs, your valuation policy must specify whether you use FBIL/CCIL published yields or a matrix price. Switching between the two mid-quarter triggers the 20%/33% deviation disclosure under the Sept-2024 SEBI circular.
